Replication report: A Spectral Theory of Grokking

Pracher, de Jong, Lieshaus, Jeffares, Rulands · arXiv 2609.26679 (Sep 2026) · independent rebuild from the paper text, CPU only

Summary. 4 of 8 checks reproduced outright and 4 partly. The exact numbers printed in the paper match to every digit, the 1/λ grokking boundary lands within 3.2% of the paper's constant, and grokking time scales with 1/(learning rate × weight decay) with log-log slope 1 away from the phase boundaries (but 0.589 if every grokking run is pooled, because runs near the boundaries slow down). Nuances: Fourier structure in the NTK mostly forms before the training set is fully fit; the ridge-residual formula is approximate for ReLU networks because SGD never reaches a stationary point; and the weight-decay dependence is weaker than proportional across seeds.

Near the decay cutoff runs grok up to ~3× slower (critical slowing, which the theory predicts), near the instability edge they slow down too, and the fastest runs hit a floor of ~700 to 1,000 updates set by the fitting stage.

The raw strength of the dominant mode then grows another 28% after the fit and plateaus, as the theory's stable fixed point predicts. Normalized shape metrics stay flat or dip slightly after the fit.
C6Theorem 1: post-fit residual is a ridge residual; weak NTK modes keep more errorproved for fixed K / stationary pointReLU nets: rel. error 0.25 (grok, 24k), 0.28 (300k); trend clearly presentPartly reproducedSmooth control (x² activation) reaches stationarity and matches to 3.21e-07; the same setup with ReLU stalls at 0.123. SGD on ReLU nets never settles (|∇obj|/|∇data| stays ≈ 0.4), so the ridge formula is a good approximation, not exact, for the paper's networks.
R1Robustness across 5 model seeds (paper uses seed 0 only)n/aη ×1.69 → s₁₀ faster ×1.66 to ×1.68; λ ×2.03 → faster ×1.42 to ×1.53Partly reproducedLearning-rate dependence matches 1/(ηλ) in every seed. Weight-decay dependence is weaker than proportional. Adding a fit-stage offset (s = α/η + C/(ηλ), from the paper's τ = ηλ(s − s_fit)) predicts held-out cells within 2.2% for every seed, but fits the full sweep worse than the plain power law (R² n/a), so it only holds locally.

Figures

Setup

Mod-23 addition, 368/161 difference split, bias-free 46→256→23 ReLU MLP (He-normal, seed 0), full-batch SGD with coupled weight decay, MSE on logits, 24,000 updates. Sweep: every second point of the paper's 84 learning rates (0.1 to 100) × 90 weight decays (5e-6 to 2e-3), 1,890 networks, ~4 h on 3 CPU cores. NTK diagnostic: mod 97, 2,376/2,377 split, η 40, λ 2.5e-5, 20,000 updates. Code, tests (18 passing) and raw results are in the repository.

Not attempted

The Transformer sweep (Fig. 4) and the NTK-alignment intervention (Fig. 6, 40 paired seeds) were left out to keep the run inside a CPU budget.
